content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the development of the embryo and fetus
Explain the functions of the placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic fluid
Describe the role of hormones during pregnancy

(gestation) is the period from implantation to birth, lasting approximately 40 weeks in humans. During this time, a single cell develops into a fully formed baby, supported by specialised structures like the placenta and amniotic sac.
All major organs begin to form
Movement felt; sex visible; viable ~24 weeks
Rapid growth; lungs mature; head down
Connected to baby by umbilical cord
Maternal and fetal blood come close but don't mix
O₂ from mother → fetus; CO₂ from fetus → mother
Glucose, amino acids, vitamins diffuse to fetus
Mother's pressure too high for fetal vessels
Opposite to normal - artery carries deoxygenated blood!
Allows fetus to move and develop muscles
Develops breast tissue; prepares for labour
Low birth weight, premature birth, SIDS
Maternal and fetal blood mix in the placenta
They come close but remain separate
The umbilical vein carries deoxygenated blood
It carries oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus
The placenta filters out all harmful substances
The fetus breathes air in the womb
Oxygen comes from mother's blood via placenta
Organ for exchange between mother and fetus
Placenta: gas exchange, nutrition, waste removal, protection
Maternal and fetal blood don't mix; exchange by diffusion
Umbilical cord: two arteries (deoxygenated), one vein (oxygenated)
Amniotic fluid: cushioning, temperature, movement, protection
Harmful substances (alcohol, nicotine, drugs) can cross placenta
Folic acid prevents neural tube defects
